programme.title: Alaska's Grizzly Gauntlet
programme.desc: Prince William Sound is home to black bears.Three thousand individuals live there, and over 100,000 in the entire territory of Alaska.Survivalist Les Stroud will take a closer look at them, and what's more, he will come face to face with them.However, before he decides to meet, he must learn more about the habits of the subjects of his research.He will be helped by someone who knows everything about the local flora and fauna.Stroud's guide spent decades observing black bears.Thanks to it, the traveler will learn what dangers he may encounter after crossing the borders of the kingdom of these predators.The expedition begins when they are preparing for the arrival of winter.They need to increase their weight because the additional protective layer is useful in hostile weather conditions.Bears are looking for food, but if they choose the wrong place, they are in serious danger.First of all, they must be vigilant - every rustle means that an unwanted companion has appeared.Viewers will see how predators deal with them.It is also worth mentioning that these animals want to be left in peace wherever they are.This is why Stroud does not enter their lairs, because a confrontation may prove painful.

programme.title: Secrets of the Penguins
programme.desc: For two years, National Geographic explorer Bertie Gregory closely studied the tight-knit communities of some of the world's most intelligent penguins.He documented behaviors and situations that had previously been difficult to capture on camera.The series proves that penguins are much closer to humans than was previously known.These unique flightless birds are brave and adventurous, and at the same time value family bonds and friendship.Thanks to their ingenuity, they can survive in the most extreme conditions Millions of years ago, a group of penguins left the icy lands, using powerful ocean currents that carried them to distant lands.Over time, these birds adapted to living in completely different places - from deserts, through the tropics, to areas inhabited by people.The fight against adversity made them one of the most intelligent birds in the world.National Geographic explorer Bertie Gregory examines their problem-solving skills, communication methods, and motivation to explore new environments.

programme.title: Super Reefs
programme.desc: As part of the Pristine Seas project, National Geographic specialists discovered pristine coral reefs.This happened during research carried out in the south of the Central Polynesian Sporades in 2009.In the period from 2015 to 2016, as a result of ocean warming, half of the corals found died.The team returned to the Pacific Ocean area in 2021.They came hoping to find even modest signs of recovery on the atolls.However, the team saw an unprecedented and spectacular recovery of coral reefs.

programme.title: One Strange Rock
programme.desc: A story about the creation and history of the planet, the laws governing it, its shape, the richness of flora and fauna, threats to the natural environment, natural wonders and surprising relationships.Actor Will Smith and people who have had the opportunity to spend time in space will talk about this extraordinary place in the universe.Accounts from astronauts including Mae Jemison, Mike Massimino, Leland Melvin and Chris Austin Hadfield will provide a completely new perspective on Earth.Director Darren Aronofsky and his film crew visited 45 countries and six continents.The photos were taken in, among others, the Arctic, the Himalayas, India and during the annual festival in Tarragona, Spain.Materials recorded on board the International Space Station were also used.In the following episodes, viewers will learn how oxygen is produced, the protective layers of the Blue Planet and the entire sequence of events that led to the creation of life.The topic of death, colonization, destruction, the search for alien forms and human intellect will also be discussed.
